name: UniFi Network
description:
The UniFi Network application's own Integration API, on one console (a UXG, UDM, Cloud Key or self-hosted Network server): its sites, each adopted device with its state and live load, and the connected clients. Unlike *UniFi Site Manager* (the cloud api.ui.com), this talks to the console itself, so it sees per-device CPU, memory and uplink numbers and the client list. Read-only: Mnemerynne only sends the fixed GET requests below.

**Setup**

1. On the console: **UniFi Network → Settings → Control Plane → Integrations** (older versions: *Settings → System → Integrations*), **Create API Key**, and copy it once. The key carries the signed-in admin's access, so create it from an admin with view-only rights if you can.
2. Change the address to the console's: `https://<console IP>/proxy/network/integration` (for a self-hosted Network server: `https://<server>:8443/proxy/network/integration`).
3. Paste the key as this API's credential. It's sent as the `X-API-KEY` header.
4. The console has a self-signed certificate: **trust (pin) it** on this page. Its name isn't the console's IP, so the host name check is off in this template; the pinned certificate is still checked on every call.
5. Set the AD group to IT and test **Application info** and **Sites** first. Every other operation needs a site's **id** from Sites.

**One console per entry.** For another console, add this preset again under another name and address.

**Clients leave out names on purpose:** on a hotel network, client names are often guests' own phone and laptop names. *Clients* keeps the type, IP, MAC, when it connected, its uplink device and its access type only. **Claude:** device names, IP and MAC addresses are internal network detail; turn Claude's switch on only if that may go to Anthropic.

**Not included:** hotspot vouchers (they hold guest access codes) and anything that changes the network (device restarts, port power cycling, client authorisation).

operations.name: Application info
operations.description: The UniFi Network application's version on this console.
example_questions: What version of UniFi Network is the console on?
Is the UniFi controller reachable?

operations.name: Sites
operations.description: The console's sites: each one's id (needed by every other operation), internal reference and name.
example_questions: Which sites are on the UniFi console?
What's the site id of the hotel network?

operations.name: Devices
operations.description: The site's adopted devices (gateways, switches, access points): id, name, model, MAC, IP, state (ONLINE, OFFLINE, UPDATING…) and features. totalCount says how many there are; page with offset if it's more than limit.
example_questions: Which UniFi devices are offline?
List the switches and access points.
What's the IP of the UXG?
How many access points does the hotel have?

operations.name: Device
operations.description: One device in full: model, firmware, state, when it was adopted and provisioned, its ports (with PoE and speed) and radios.
example_questions: What firmware is the lobby access point on?
Which ports on the core switch are up?
Is PoE on for port 12 of the switch?

operations.name: Device statistics
operations.description: One device's latest numbers: uptime, CPU and memory use, load averages, uplink speed and traffic, and per-radio TX retries.
example_questions: How busy is the gateway's CPU?
How much memory is the UXG using?
What's the uplink speed of the lobby AP?
Is the access point retrying a lot?
How long has the switch been up?

operations.name: Clients
operations.description: Connected clients: type (WIRED, WIRELESS, VPN…), id, IP, MAC, when it connected, the device it's connected through and its access type. Names are left out (guests' devices). totalCount says how many are connected; page with offset.
example_questions: How many clients are connected?
How many devices are on the UniFi network right now?
Which access point is 172.27.22.50 connected through?
What IP does MAC aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff have?
How many wired clients are there?
